source: Kolling, Behrens, Mars, Rushworth (2012) Neural mechanisms of foraging
finding: fMRI two-stage task. Choice to search for a new option depends on encounter value (low favours search), search value (average of alternatives, high favours search) and search cost. dACC BOLD rose with search value and fell with encounter value. vmPFC tracked chosen value only when engaging. People were biased against searching ('forage readiness').
numbers: Search-value slope steeper on search than engage trials: t(17)=-2.54, p=0.021 (implies about 18 subjects; N not stated in text). 12 pre-learned values, 6 boxed alternatives, 3 search-cost levels.
limits: Small sample, correlational fMRI, small learned value set. Beta weights only in figures. dACC role later contested by Shenhav 2014 (difficulty confound).
agent_relevance: Core S6 rule: leave when current yield falls below the average of alternatives minus cost. But humans under-search relative to normative gain, so a leave trigger needs a bias term for persistence.

source: Shenhav, Straccia, Cohen, Botvinick (2014) Anterior cingulate engagement in a foraging context reflects choice difficulty, not foraging value
finding: Replicated the Kolling task (Exp 1) then built a second design (Exp 2) that decoupled foraging value from difficulty. dACC tracked choice difficulty, not foraging value. In Kolling's design the true indifference point was relative forage value about 1.65, not 0, so 'difficulty' was mis-specified and correlated with foraging value.
numbers: Exp1 N=15, Exp2 N=14. Corrected difficulty vs foraging value Spearman rho=0.80. Exp2 difficulty t(13)=2.8 p=0.014; foraging value t(13)=0.47 p=0.64; direct contrast p=0.046; holds controlling RT (p=0.034).
limits: Small N. Does not refute the behavioural leave rule, only the neural interpretation of dACC. Kolling 2016 rebuts: difficulty insufficient, not absent.
agent_relevance: A partial failed replication of the neural claim. Do not build the schema on 'a conflict or value signal tells you to leave'. The behavioural rule stands separately.

source: Kolling, Wittmann, Behrens, Boorman, Mars, Rushworth (2016) Value, search, persistence and model updating in anterior cingulate cortex
finding: Authors' reply to the difficulty critique. Their design shared less than 2.5% variance between search value and difficulty; search value survived controls for difficulty and log RT in dACC (peak near MNI 4,36,26). dACC also responded to model updating, not just surprise.
numbers: Variance shared by search value and difficulty <2.5% by design. Difficulty and logRT effects only marginal and late.
limits: A review: no new sample sizes, relies on fMRI interpretation. Two camps still disagree.
agent_relevance: Supports treating 'search value' and 'difficulty' as separate triggers: leaving because alternatives look good is not the same as leaving because the choice is hard.

source: Hayden, Pearson, Platt (2011) Neuronal basis of sequential foraging decisions in a patchy environment
finding: Two monkeys in a virtual patch-leaving task. They stayed 2.2 s longer than the marginal value theorem predicted but earned 97.2% of the best-fit rate-maximising reward. dACC firing ramped up with time in patch and leaving happened when it reached a threshold that rose with travel time.
numbers: 2 monkeys, 102 dACC neurons (49 with positive ramp). Stay value 306 ul falling 19 ul per choice. Residence time vs travel time beta=1.247 (P<0.0001). Overstay 2.2 s (P<0.01). MVT beat delay-discounting model, Akaike weight ratio about 1.3e52. Leave-trial firing threshold did not differ by earliness (P=0.88).
limits: Two animals. Threshold crossing probably downstream of dACC. Authors' own stats have a noted inconsistency (one P value).
agent_relevance: Near-optimal but slightly over-staying is the baseline pattern. A leave rule that is 'about right, a bit sticky' matches biology. Threshold rises when travel (switch) cost is higher.

source: Constantino & Daw (2015) Learning the opportunity cost of time in a patch-foraging task
finding: Humans overharvested (left at lower reward rate than optimal) but adapted thresholds to travel time and depletion. Learning-model comparison: a recency-weighted average-reward rule (MVT-style) beat TD, TD(lambda) and R-learning. Overharvesting mostly disappears with a risk-sensitivity term.
numbers: Exp1 N=11+11, Exp2 N=30 (52 recruited, 47 analysed). Earnings about 9-10% below optimal. MVT vs TD exceedance prob 0.999 (expected freq 0.83 Exp1, 0.85 Exp2). Intercept overharvest t20=-4.87 (Exp1), t20=-7.48 (Exp2); with risk sensitivity t20=-1.33 p=0.2 and t20=-1.71 p=0.10. Best constant-hazard policy 25-33% below optimal. Threshold adapts: depletion F(1,25)=82, travel F(1,25)=42.1.
quote: exits when expected reward falls below it
limits: Small samples, virtual apple trees, 14-min blocks. Thresholds significantly low in only 1 of 3 Exp1 conditions tested; text states significance in the long-travel condition only.
agent_relevance: Rate-comparison with a running average (not a fixed count or discounting) is the better description. For S6: track a running yield average and compare current yield to it; a fixed step cap loses 25-33%.

source: Wolfe (2013) When is it time to move to the next raspberry bush? Foraging rules in human visual search
finding: Six berry-picking experiments, about 10 observers each. Uniform patches: leaving matched MVT. Mixed patch quality with slow travel: left too early. No colour cue (Exp 6): leaving did not follow a rate rule; observers used patch-wise all-or-nothing picking.
numbers: Exp2 exhaustive instruction hit rate 68% to 83% and longer stays. Exp4 fast travel 0.76 vs MVT 0.75 berries/s; slow travel 0.66 vs 0.45 (left early). Exp5 0.81 vs 0.85 fast; slow left early.
limits: About 10 observers per experiment, repeated observers. Visual search, not value learning.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: the average-rate rule works for uniform depleting sources, fails with mixed quality or no clear quality cue. For the agent, mixed-quality sub-tasks need a quality estimate before the rate rule is usable. Instructions ('find every one') shift stay time strongly.

source: Harhen & Bornstein (2023) Overharvesting in human patch foraging reflects rational structure learning and adaptive planning
finding: Overharvesting is explained as rational learning of a multi-modal environment plus uncertainty-adaptive discounting. Humans (N=116) overharvested overall, more early than late, and only in poor and neutral patches; on rich patches they were near MVT-optimal.
numbers: df=115 so N=116. Overharvest overall t(115)=3.88 P=.00018; first two vs last two blocks t(115)=3.27 P=.0014. Poor t=6.92, neutral t=9.00, rich t=1.38 P=.17. Stay longer rich vs neutral t=19.77, neutral vs poor t=12.57.
limits: One task family (space-mining), 5 six-minute blocks. Model fit details not read.
agent_relevance: Over-staying shrinks with experience and is largest where the source is poor, so an agent that has seen the distribution of source quality should leave earlier than a naive agent. Cold-start is the risky phase.

source: Kane, Bornstein, Shenhav, Wilson, Daw, Cohen (2019) Rats exhibit similar biases in foraging and intertemporal choice tasks
finding: Rats overharvested in all tested conditions. A quasi-hyperbolic discounting model fitted per rat explained both foraging and intertemporal choice, a common myopic mechanism. Earlier attempts to explain overharvesting with discounting from intertemporal tasks had failed.
numbers: n=8 rats in four experiments, a separate n=8 for the travel-time experiment. Overharvest beta=3.396 trials (SE .176, t(6.96)=19.27, p<.001). Longer travel gave longer stays beta=1.893 trials (t=6.04). Overharvesting did not differ between 10 s and 30 s travel (p=0.088).
limits: Rats, small n, sucrose reward. Quasi-hyperbolic model is flexible.
agent_relevance: Overstay is a robust bias (myopia plus ignoring opportunity cost). If the LLM inherits human-like persistence, S6 needs an explicit counter-bias, not only a neutral threshold.

source: Lenow, Constantino, Daw, Phelps (2017) Chronic and acute stress promote overexploitation in serial decision making
finding: Higher cortisol response and higher perceived stress predicted lower exit thresholds, meaning staying longer (overexploitation). Group (cold pressor vs warm) alone did not predict behaviour.
numbers: N=65 (29 control, 36 stress). Cortisol manipulation check t(64)=-4.58. Log cortisol change beta=-0.37 t(61)=-2.04 p<.05. Perceived Stress Scale beta=-0.49 t(61)=-2.91 p<.01. MVT thresholds 6.52 (short) and 5.31 (long travel). Environment effect on deviation p=0.81.
limits: Between-subjects, single cortisol measure, group effect null. Author list in this line is from memory, not verified on the page.
agent_relevance: Moderator: pressure raises persistence. A scaffold used under token or time pressure may over-stay, so budget warnings should push toward leaving, not toward cramming.

source: Dopamine modulates dynamic decision-making during foraging (2020, J Neurosci)
finding: Humans decide when to leave depleting patches by weighing foreground (current) and background (environment) reward rates, both independently. Cabergoline (D2 agonist) changed the background-rate effect: in poor environments people left patches much earlier. Every individual stayed longer than MVT-optimal across patch types.
numbers: Study 1: 40 volunteers (39 analysed, mean age 24). Study 2: 30 older adults (mean age 69; 29 analysed), double-blind placebo crossover.
limits: Exact effect sizes not extracted (abstract, methods and one results paragraph read). Older sample for drug study.
agent_relevance: Two separate inputs to the leave rule: current yield and the environment's average. An agent should keep both explicitly; a hidden or wrong background estimate shifts leaving.

source: Apathy and compulsivity on planning and stopping in sequential decision-making (2022, PLOS Biology)
finding: Large online sample on a sequential search task. Apathy predicted 'decision inertia' (repeating search because already searched), compulsivity predicted cost insensitivity and self-reported overchasing. Individual differences in persistence are measurable.
numbers: Confirmation sample N=756 (discovery 449). Apathy to inertia mean=0.066 (1-sided CI lower bound 0.005). Cost insensitivity mean=0.061 missed significance in confirmation (CI lower -0.006) though significant in discovery. Overchasing OR=1.224; avoidance OR=1.423.
limits: Self-report and online. Cost-insensitivity result did not replicate within the paper. First 100k characters of a 292k page read.
agent_relevance: Decision inertia is a distinct failure: more previous searches make another search more likely. For the agent: count consecutive attempts of one operator and treat the count as a risk, not as evidence of progress.

source: Kilpatrick, Davidson, El Hady (2021) Uncertainty drives deviations in normative foraging decision strategies
finding: Bayesian forager that infers patch yield from encounters leaves when certainty or estimated yield falls under a threshold. Uncertainty makes it overharvest initially poor patches and underharvest initially rich ones relative to MVT.
numbers: Theory paper; no human sample. Departures under slow depletion are marked by reduced uncertainty.
limits: Normative model, not tested on behaviour here. Abstract read.
agent_relevance: Predicts both directions of error, so 'always leave earlier' is wrong: leave earlier on poor sources, stay longer on rich ones.

source: Kilpatrick & El Hady (2026) Resource depletion accelerates rate learning but not composition learning in patch foraging
finding: Hierarchical Bayesian forager. Best departure rule depends on patch variability: count prey when variability is low; time the gaps between prey once variability exceeds about a quarter. Learning the environment gives clearly higher intake than learning a rule from reward alone.
numbers: Variability threshold about 25%. 35 pages, 10 figures. Reward-maximising and information-seeking strategies diverge, so underharvest of rich patches early.
limits: Abstract only read. Theory, no empirical test. Holds if depletion assumptions are not far off.
agent_relevance: Which stopping signal to use (count of attempts vs time between successes) depends on how variable the source is. Candidate design choice for S6: use gaps between hits when yields are noisy.

source: Lottem et al. (2018) Activation of serotonin neurons promotes active persistence in a probabilistic foraging task
finding: Mice (n=16) left sites at a reward rate that tracked their own average reward rate (correlation p<0.001; difference from average n.s., Wilcoxon p>0.05). Optogenetic activation of dorsal raphe serotonin neurons increased active persistence before giving up.
numbers: n=16 mice. Leave rate vs average rate correlation p<0.001; difference not significant (p>0.05).
limits: Mice; exact opto effect sizes not extracted. Claims about 5-HT beyond foraging not tested.
agent_relevance: Mice approach the average-rate rule closely, while persistence is a tunable parameter. Suggests a persistence knob can be separate from the rate estimate.

source: Individuals with adverse childhood experiences explore less and underweight reward feedback (2022, PNAS)
finding: Preregistered foraging study. Adults with four or more adverse childhood experiences explored less (stayed in the depleting patch) and, contrary to prediction, underweighted recent feedback.
numbers: N=145 (47 with 4+ ACEs, 98 with fewer).
limits: Authors' hypothesis on recent-feedback weighting was refuted. Observational, retrospective ACE report. Only abstract read.
agent_relevance: Individual and history differences move stay time; the preregistered prediction on feedback weighting failed, so a 'recent-feedback' explanation of persistence is not safe.

source: Neural evidence of switch processes during semantic and phonetic foraging in human memory (2023, PNAS)
finding: fMRI of fluency tasks treated as foraging in memory. The paper cites earlier work (Hills et al. 2012) that people who leave clusters closer to the MVT point (inter-item time near their average) produce more words. It tests brain activity at switches.
numbers: N=30 (24 for cerebellar analyses). About 44 correct in category fluency and 34 in letter fluency per 3 min. Similarity-based vs participant-designated switches agree about 60%.
limits: MVT adherence is cited from earlier work, not tested here.
agent_relevance: Patch-leaving logic extends to internal search. Leave a train of thought when the gap between new useful ideas exceeds the running average.

source: Fonseca, Rios, Quijano, Giraldo (2025) World models unlock optimal foraging strategies in reinforcement learning agents
finding: Not an LLM. A model-based RL agent (DreamerV2) takes step counts per patch close to the MVT optimum in at least 3 of 4 patch-distance scenarios, and tends to overstay slightly, like animals. A model-free PPO agent diverges strongly and the MVT value falls outside its interquartile range.
numbers: 4 patch spacings (3, 5, 7, 9 cells). MVT optimum inside +/-1 quartile for 3 of 4 scenarios for DreamerV2; PPO in none of 4 (per text).
limits: Grid world, single environment, no human data, results shown as box plots. arXiv preprint.
agent_relevance: Planning with a learned model brings leaving near the optimum; reactive policies do not. Supports giving the agent an explicit forecast of future yield before the leave decision.

source: Lacosse, Duarte, Todd, McNamee (2026) Emerging human-like strategies for semantic memory foraging in LLMs
finding: Llama-3 models (1B, 3B, 8B, 70B) on animal fluency, compared to 699 human lists. LLM transition structure matched humans but LLMs exploit clusters more and switch less than humans.
numbers: Switch ratio mean 0.55 humans vs 0.40 LLMs (Mann-Whitney p<0.0001). Transition matrix correlation Spearman 0.701 (p<0.001). 681 human and 2285 LLM sequences after filter. Probability mass moves to between-category tokens at a switch in Llama-3.3-70B (d=0.144).
limits: NeurIPS 2025 mechanistic interpretability workshop, preliminary. Only animals, only Llama-3. No test of the MVT rule itself.
agent_relevance: Direct LLM evidence of the over-staying direction: models switch less than humans. Supports an external leave trigger in S6.

source: Leckie, Todd, Foster (2026) Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models
finding: Interpretability on semantic fluency: switching is more likely as the strongest internal activations lose items from the current category, analogous to patch foraging. Steering vectors raise or lower the switch rate causally.
numbers: Two studies; no numbers in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only read. Quantitative effect sizes not seen. v1 posted 28 Sep 2026.
agent_relevance: There may be an internal depletion signal in LLMs, but it is not reliably acted on without a prompt-level trigger.

source: Binz & Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: GPT-3 outperformed humans in a multi-armed bandit but showed no signature of directed exploration. On short horizons its regret matched humans.
numbers: Short-horizon regret vs humans t(5566)=-0.043, P=.97.
limits: Bandit exploration, not patch leaving. Older model (GPT-3).
agent_relevance: Adjacent evidence only. Absence of directed exploration means LLMs do not leave an exploited option to gather information unless forced.

source: Krishnamurthy, Harris, Foster, Zhang, Slivkins (2024) Can large language models explore in-context?
finding: GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama2 in bandit problems did not reliably explore. Only one tested configuration worked: GPT-4 with chain-of-thought and an externally summarised history of sufficient statistics.
numbers: 3 models; 1 configuration with satisfactory exploration. Accepted at NeurIPS 2024.
limits: Abstract page only. Bandit exploration, not depletion. Metrics not seen.
agent_relevance: The one thing that worked was an external summary of past yields. That matches a design where S6 receives a computed yield-so-far summary, not the raw trace.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Do NOT think that much for 2+3=? On the overthinking of o1-like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models spend large compute on easy problems for little gain. A self-training method shortens reasoning without hurting accuracy on GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA and AIME.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract only. Overthinking is a stopping problem but not framed as MVT.
agent_relevance: LLM analogue of overharvesting: staying with a depleting reasoning path. Gives a measured case where leaving earlier costs no accuracy.

source: Qian & Liu (2025) Scent of Knowledge: Optimizing search-enhanced reasoning with information foraging (InForage)
finding: RL framework using information foraging theory; rewards the quality of intermediate retrievals. Reports gains over baselines on QA, multi-hop reasoning and a real-time web QA dataset. NeurIPS 2025 spotlight.
numbers: Benchmark scores not seen (abstract page only).
limits: The foraging idea is a design metaphor; no patch-leaving rule is tested against MVT.
agent_relevance: Shows the foraging frame has been used to train search agents, but evidence for the leave rule itself is missing.

source: Azzopardi & Roegiest (2026) Information farming: from berry picking to berry growing
finding: Conceptual argument that generative AI shifts users from foraging in others' sources to cultivating their own. Predicts less transient foraging.
numbers: No data.
limits: Position paper.
agent_relevance: Boundary on relevance: when the agent writes its own sources, 'leave a depleting source' may apply less.

source: Charnov (1976) Optimal foraging, the marginal value theorem
finding: Founding result: leave a patch when the instantaneous intake rate falls to the long-run average rate of the environment, including travel time. Not opened this session.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Assumes full knowledge of the environment, depleting patches, rate maximisation.
agent_relevance: Origin of the S6 rule.

source: Davidson & El Hady (2019) Foraging as an evidence accumulation process
finding: Downloaded but not read this session. Frames patch leaving as evidence accumulation to a bound, a bridge between the MVT and drift-diffusion models.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Link to the evidence-accumulation subfield in this run.
